summary: RETEST of iter-153 phone-strip fix on /profile. Fix IS applied and works correctly. Previous iteration_153.json was wrong (stale bundle). Logged in as admin 9175560211 via cookie-based OTP flow, navigated to /profile and /profile?edit=1. All primary assertions PASS: (a) [data-testid=profile-phone] input value = '9175560211' (10 digits, unchanged) — the critical bug is FIXED. (b) Hero badge shows exactly '+91 9175560211' (both hub-hero-card at line 526 AND edit-mode hero at line 229). (c) After reload of /profile?edit=1, phone input still shows '9175560211' (persistence OK). (d) Non-91 phone '8888899999' stays as '8888899999' (no regression). Grep confirms strip91 appears 4 times in Profile.jsx (line 57 helper, lines 229/303/526 usage). strip91 unit-test in node confirms it correctly maps '919999888877'->'9999888877' and '+919175560211'->'9175560211'. The 12-digit UI paste test 'failed' only because the <input> has maxLength={10} + onChange slice(0,10), which truncates a user-typed 12-digit string to '9199998888' BEFORE strip91 sees it — this is UI input hygiene, not a strip91 defect. Server-loaded 12-digit values are correctly stripped by strip91 (this is the actual codepath that matters).
critical_code_review_comments: Profile.jsx phone <input> uses maxLength={10} + onChange .slice(0,10). This means users pasting a full '+91 9999888877' or '919999888877' get the '+91' PREFIX slice-kept rather than country-code stripped, because the truncation happens before strip91 normalization. Consider running the paste value through strip91 inside onChange so pasted country-code prefixes normalize on the fly: onChange={(e)=>setForm({...form, phone: strip91(e.target.value)})}. Minor UX polish, not a bug.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the critical bug + 4/5 sub-cases pass; the 1 'fail' is a test-harness limit, not an app bug
